paragraphs: Hyman mentions him in Jerusalem Talmud Sotah, chapter 3, end of halakhah 7, speaking in Rabbi Acha’s name in the name of Rabbi Lazar, that women of priestly families are permitted to go abroad.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The Guggenheimer digital text of Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 3:7 has Dosa of Malchiya followed by Acha in Lazar’s name. Hyman’s wording instead explicitly makes Dosa speak in Acha’s name. The translation follows Hyman’s supplied chain without treating the digital asyndetic sequence as a proven identical transmission.

The whole Guggenheimer Sotah 3:7 paragraph fully writes Rabbi Dosa of Malchiya, Rabbi Acha and Rabbi Lazar. It places Dosa and Acha next to each other before the report in Lazar’s name; Hyman explicitly has Dosa reporting Acha. The full local titles are supported, while the transmission difference remains as stated in the retained note; no identical chain or teacher relationship is admitted.
